messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert: inference error-rate >10% and p95 token latency spike for hosted us-west-1a. Trigger: repeated ECONNRESETs between proxy fleet and inference pods. Paging @rachel (primary on-call).
rachel: saw alerts at 2026-03-17T04:00Z. Dashboards: request failures concentrated in us-west-1a, backend 502s + connection resets. Control plane healthy.
rachel: starting investigation026-03-17T04:01Z 026-03-17T04:10Z.
rory: network team here. Quick check: VPC flow logs show large number of RSTs and SNAT port exhaustion spikes from NAT gateway in subnet-1a. Also seeing route table changes around the same timeframe.
sam: confirmed tcpdump on a victim host shows many SYNs with no SYN-ACKs, then resets. NAT gateway metrics show ephemeral port usage at 98%.
rachel: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) steer traffic off us-west-1a by updating regional weights in Route53 (us-west-1a -> 50%, us-west-1b -> 30%, eu-west-1 -> 20%); 2) spin up additional nat-gw replacements in us-west-1a (if possible) and enable port-overlap across AZs; 3) temporarily reduce batch sizes and disable prefetching on 1a to lower connection churn.
tasha: i'll take DNS weight change. Also will lower ALB connection drain timeout to 10s to allow faster cutover.
infra-bot: Creating incident INC-7001 and auto-adding runbook 'az-nat-port-saturation'.
leo: customer impact: several customers reporting 502s on hosted API. No full outage but degraded experience. CS alerted.
cs-bot: CS ticket CS-4640 created and flagged for enterprise outreach.
rachel: running `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filters Name=tag:env,Values=prod Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-1a` to list gateways.
rory: I see two NATs in 1a; both at high port utilization. Could be due to high ephemeral connection churn from batchers + grpc keepalives. We'll request AWS to increase port capacity and check route-table flaps.
sam: kernel dmesg on host-07 shows this: ```
Mar 17 03:59:58 host-07 kernel: tcp: too many orphaned sockets; dropping conn
Mar 17 03:59:59 host-07 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
rachel: conntrack exhaustion would align with NAT port exhaustion symptoms. For immediate relief: (a) increase conntrack table size via sysctl on affected hosts (temporary); (b) toggle kube-proxy conntrack sync to reduce churn; (c) apply traffic steering to reduce new connections to 1a.
tasha: DNS weights adjusted: us-west-1a 50 -> 50, us-west-1b 30 -> 30, eu-west-1 20 -> 20 (making sure we don't send them all to one place). TTL set to 20s for quick iteration.
infra-bot: route propagation note: Route53 update submitted by tasha at 2026-03-17T04:08Z.
leo: after weight change and conntrack tweak, observed error-rate drop from 11.6% -> 4.1% within 90s. p95 latency from 5.8s -> 2.1s.
rachel: adding short-run fixes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on a few hot hosts; also applied `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` to recycle TIME_WAIT ports. We'll track side effects.
sam: note: be careful with tcp_tw_reuse on ephemeral-ports with NAT; ok for short term.
rory: opened AWS SR requesting NAT port allocation increase, check for route table churn, and request VPC flow logs for the suspect window. SR ref: SR-2026-452.
leo: CS comms drafted: "We observed transient degradation for customers in us-west-1a between 04:00-04:30 UTC. Traffic was partially routed to other AZs and EU region while we mitigated. Some requests may have returned 502/error. We're investigating root cause and will follow with postmortem."
infra-bot: severity set to S2 at 2026-03-17T04:20Z after mitigation.
rachel: handing off to rory for overnight follow-up. Handoff notes: suspected root cause: NAT gateway / conntrack port exhaustion amplified by route table change and connection churn from large batchers. Need AWS confirmation and plan for either increasing NAT capacity or adding per-AZ EIPs and mid-tier proxies. Handoff ETA: 2026-03-17T10:00Z UTC.
rory: taking over. Next steps: (1) gather host-level dmesg + conntrack dumps; (2) coordinate with AWS on NAT capacity and route-table history; (3) design permanent mitigations: autoscaler rate limits, batcher backpressure, and per-AZ NAT scaling.
leo: action items logged: rachel -> attach instance IDs + pod map to INC-7001; rory -> AWS SR + flow logs; sam -> tcpdump archive; tasha -> monitor Route53 weights and revert when stable.
rachel: added instances: i-0d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e,i-0e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d (partial sample).
sam: tcpdump excerpt: many retransmits and frequent short-lived connections, likely from aggressive client retries + small batch keepalive.
leo: customer success will follow up with personalized messages for those affected.
rachel: final note to runbook: avoid simultaneous conntrack tweaks across whole fleet; do targeted host updates. Prefer gradual scaling of NAT capacity over mass sysctl changes.
infra-bot: Incident thread set to update-only mode and will remain open until SR closure.
cs-bot: CS follow-up scheduled in 24h.
rory: leaving a checklist for postmortem: timeline, root-cause analysis (conntrack + nat), config changes, recommended autoscaler throttles, and alert tuning to detect conntrack high-water sooner.
rachel: signing off active pager. If error-rate creeps back up, the pager will re-alert.
IncidentBot: Active paging closed but thread will accept updates."
